recommendations.regimenLabel: Correct the metabolic cause + supportive care
steps: Find and correct the cause — glucose, Na, Ca, uraemia, hypercapnia, ammonia, drugs, hypoxia, sepsis.
Empirical thiamine in at-risk patients; naloxone if opioid suspected.
Treat the underlying organ failure; review/stop offending drugs.

drugRefs.dose: 100 mg IV (higher, e.g. 500 mg three times daily, if Wernicke encephalopathy suspected)
drugRefs.freq: give before/with any glucose in at-risk patients
drugRefs.why: Empirical replacement in malnourished/alcohol-dependent patients to prevent or treat Wernicke encephalopathy; give before glucose to avoid precipitating it.

drugRefs.freq: repeat every 2–3 min, titrated to respiration
drugRefs.why: Reverses opioid-induced depressed consciousness where opioid toxicity is a possible contributor; both diagnostic and therapeutic.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Coma and Metabolic Encephalopathy
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Confusion, Delirium and the Encephalopathies

decision.label: Identify and correct the metabolic cause

confirm: Diffuse alteration of consciousness without focal deficit; asterixis, myoclonus. Identify the metabolic cause.

investigations.test: Glucose, U&E, Ca, LFTs, ammonia, ABG
